figures.finding: Canadian features are made mostly in English: of C$460M of theatrical feature production in 2024/25, English-language work was C$320M and French-language C$140M.

sources.said: Overall, the volume of production declined by 3.2% from $475 million in 2023/24 to $460 million in 2024/25. French-language production increased by 35% to $140 million, while English-language production decreased by 13.8% to $320 million.

figures.finding: Ontario (Toronto) leads: Ontario-based producers made 52% of Canadian feature production in 2024/25, and across all film and television production Ontario took 36.3% of 2023 industry revenue, British Columbia 34.1% and Quebec 22.7%.

sources.said: Ontario-based producers accounted for the largest share (52%) of film production in 2024/25, with $238 million in production volume, followed by Quebec ($172 million), British Columbia ($34 million), Atlantic Canada ($11 million) and the Prairie Provinces and Territories ($5 million).
Industry revenue remained largely concentrated in 2023, with the vast majority of total industry revenue coming from Ontario (36.3%), British Columbia (34.1%) and Quebec (22.7%).

figures.finding: Under the CMPA-DGC Standard Agreement 2026-2028 (every DGC district but B.C. and Quebec) a theatrical feature's director is paid at least a weekly rate by the budget's tier, with a mandatory rights acquisition fee of 90% of it, for a guaranteed period of prep and shoot: from 1 January 2026, CAD 13,726 a week for 16 weeks in tier A (CAD 17,593,418 and over), 12,375 for 15 (B), 11,506 for 14 (C) and 9,779 for 10 (D, from CAD 3,500,001), and in tier F (under CAD 3,500,000) 2% of the total budget plus 0.75%, for 8 weeks; the tiers' bounds and tiers A to D's rates rise in 2027 and 2028.

figures.applies: Canada outside B.C. and Quebec, theatrical features, from 1 January 2026 to the agreement's end (31 December 2028; past it the last year's are kept, person.markets.model). The weekly rate and its rights fee pay the guaranteed prep and shoot; the Director's cut weeks (DR9.04) aren't read as days beyond the guaranteed period, whose daily rate is a quarter of the weekly (DR16.02). A budget of exactly the dollar between tier F's 'under' and tier D's start is read as F's. Tier E has no theatrical band.

sources.said: DR9.04 Minimum Time Allowance The Director shall be allowed at least the following minimum time allowances for the preparation of the Director’s cut: (a) For Theatrical Motion Pictures: i. Budgeted at one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) or less, four (4) weeks after completion of the assemblage of sequences provided for in Article DR9.08; ii. Budgeted at two million dollars ($2,000,000.00) or less but more than one million dollars ($1,000,000), six (6) weeks after the completion of assemblage of sequences provided for in Article DR9.08; iii. Budgeted at more than two million dollars ($2,000,000.00), eight (8) weeks after the completion of assemblage of sequences provided for in Article DR9.08. … (c) For Episodic Television Series: i. having a running time of thirty (30) minutes or less, within one (1) Day plus time and the opportunity to make changes, if necessary, but not to exceed one (1) more Day after the completion of assemblage of sequences provided for in Article DR9.08; ii. having a running time of sixty (60) minutes or less, but more than thirty (30) minutes, within three (3) Days after the completion of assemblage of sequences provided for in Article DR9.08. … DR15.00 TIER LEVELS AND BUDGETS DEFINED Tiers apply from January 1, 2026 until the expiration of this Agreement. DR15.01 The minimum rates for Directors under Articles DR16.00, DR17.00 and DR18.00 have been divided into six (6) tier levels based on the type of Production and the total Budget of that Production as set out below. The Budget range reflects the total Budget (including above and below the line) in Canadian dollars. … DR16.02 Daily Rate The minimum daily rate for additional Days worked beyond the Director’s guaranteed period or for daily engagement, where permissible, shall be one-fourth (1/4th) of the Weekly Rate payable for the particular type of Motion Picture. … DR19.02 Additional Use - Theatrical Motion Pictures (a) Tiers A - D The Producer shall make a mandatory payment of ninety percent (90%) of the applicable Director’s minimum rate at the time of Production. … (b) Tier F For Theatrical Motion Pictures in Tier F, the minimum rate shall be 2% of the total Budget plus an additional .75% mandatory rights acquisition fee
